description: Multi-head attention forward. Q is [batch, heads, seqlen_q, head_dim]; K and V share seqlen_k.

heads_kv.description: KV head count. Equal to heads is MHA, 1 is MQA, anything between is GQA.

alignment.description: Which corner the causal diagonal is anchored at. Only a distinct problem where the mask is causal and seqlen_q < seqlen_k; the constraint below pins it to top_left everywhere else, so the sweep does not spend half its budget measuring each shape twice. An engine that serves one anchor and refuses the other is removed from a comparison by the corpus rather than by a measurement, which is why this is a declared axis rather than a fixed choice.

generate_stats.description: The training forward: also write the softmax statistics (logsumexp) the backward pass consumes.

form.description: Which optional attributes and tensors the graph binds (RFC 0019 §6.7, absent is not zero, and §6.8 rule 9: a model must tolerate any optional feature a valid graph leaves unbound). One aspect varies per graph from the plain baseline, so every optional input appears both present and absent without crossing them all. plain states the scale and binds nothing optional; scale_unset leaves the scale unstated; scale_tensor gives it as a pass-by-value tensor; dropout adds Philox dropout with an INT64 seed and offset; padded adds per-batch seq_len_q and seq_len_kv; ragged packs Q, O and the statistics through one offset tensor and K and V through another (compact THD, no length tensors); bias adds an additive [1, 1, seqlen_q, seqlen_k] bias; sink adds one FLOAT sink logit per query head. A --model-shapes file with no `q.form` column reads every row as plain; a column left empty in a row is refused.

// regime_label: The populations a corpus is reported per, as RFC 0019.13 §11.2's regret table needs them.
Phase: decode is one query token against a cache and is memory bound on that cache;
prefill is the whole prompt at once and is compute bound on the score matrix. They are the
same operation and entirely different problems, which is why they are anchored as separate
archetypes rather than as one range over seqlen_q. Cross attention (more queries than keys)
draws its two sequences from different tensors, so it varies independently of the rest --
the constraint above excludes it today, and the clause stays so that lifting the constraint
does not silently file cross-attention under 'append'.
Grouping (mha/gqa/mqa) is the third facet: how many query heads share one KV head decides
how much of the KV cache a wavefront re-reads, which is the whole difference between a
decode that is bandwidth bound and one that is not. It is a label rather than a bucket
because what matters is heads_kv relative to heads, not its magnitude.
// form_label: The optional aspects a graph binds, reported as a facet column of its own and counted by --form-floor.
Not part of the regime label above: forms cross every regime, so joining them in would multiply
the regime names (and break the quotas keyed on them) instead of adding a column.
Each non-plain value is one clause on the declared `form` parameter, so a focused search pins it.
// kernel_catalog: How a descriptor pack's metadata reads back as a point. The pack names its fields whatever
the kernel author named them; this is the only place those spellings appear, so a new pack
vocabulary is a declaration edit rather than a code change. A descriptor missing any mapped
field carries no geometry and contributes nothing -- which is how pointwise_add and the
shipped tiled_attention are excluded without naming them anywhere.
A pack value with no entry under `enums` is skipped and counted, never guessed: a pack in
fp8 read as bf16 would produce a corpus of graphs the engine does not serve, labelled as
`constants` answers for a parameter the pack vocabulary has no field for at all. These
packs record `causal` without recording which corner the diagonal is anchored at, because
every kernel in them anchors it top-left; saying so here is what lets the builder resolve
an argument no descriptor supplies. A parameter mapped under `metadata` is refused here,
so a constant can never overwrite what a descriptor actually said.

graph_builder.// types: Operands carry the declared dtype; accumulation and the score matrix are fp32. Left to default, compute follows io and every fp16/bf16 graph is uniform half precision, which hip-kernel-provider's SdpaFwdPlanBuilder refuses outright ('Compute data type must be FLOAT') and the ingestor engines decline at graph_match -- a live-engine corpus then admits nothing, indistinguishable from naming an engine that does not exist. The training forward's softmax statistics are fp32.
graph_builder.// layout: BSHD: dims stay (B, H, S, D) and the layout lives in the strides, token-major, as the shipped bundles lay them out. Not row-major: strides_of would give BHSD, and rocKE's dense kernels take no stride kernargs -- stride_q_tok is baked as Hq*D -- so their matcher (hasBshdStrides) declines every BHSD graph, and a live-engine corpus for rocKE comes out empty. AITER serves BSHD too, so this keeps both engines in the contest.
graph_builder.// scale: attnScale is the plain form's stated scale, not left to the schema's optional: rocKE's dense matcher declines a graph with no attn_scale_value (the scale is a required f32 kernarg and guessing 1/sqrt(D) is what it refuses to do), so a corpus that was all scale_unset would empty a rocKE corpus. 1/sqrt(head_dim) is the standard scale and what the shipped bundles carry. The other forms leave it out (scale_unset, scale_tensor) or keep it (the rest), and the live-engine oracle drops the forms an engine refuses, which is how rocKE's corpus stays free of them.
graph_builder.// form: One optional aspect per graph, everything else as the plain graph has it. The conventions are hipDNN's own: seq_len_q and seq_len_kv are INT32 [B, 1, 1, 1] (SdpaFwdNode::validateSeqLenTensor); the offset tensors of a ragged operand are INT32 [B+1, 1, 1, 1] (detail::validateIndexTensor; SdpaVllmFormTestGraphs.hpp makeVllmGraph); the sink is one FLOAT logit per query head, [1, Hq, 1, 1] (validateSinkToken); the scale tensor is a single-element pass-by-value tensor (validateScalarParameter), given as a runtime parameter whose default is the plain form's scale; the bias takes Q's dtype and dims [1, 1, seqlen_q, seqlen_k], row-major (the node's ATTN_MASK rule: last two dims equal seq_q and seq_kv, or 1). The dropout seed and offset are INT64 [1, 1, 1, 1] device tensors as the test SDK builds them (RaggedSdpaDensifyTestGraphs.hpp withPhiloxDropout); the frontend states no rule for them, so that one is the test SDK's convention, not a validated one. ragged is makeVllmGraph's compact THD form with a ragged query and KV: Q and O share one offset tensor with multiplier heads*head_dim, the statistics the same tensor with multiplier heads (so ragged statistics are token-major, [seqlen_q*heads, 1, heads, 1], as there), K and V another with multiplier heads_kv*head_dim; no length tensors and no padding mask; the dims stay the padded (B, H, max_len, D) ones. Each multiplier is the tensor's token stride, which the BSHD strides above make heads*head_dim.

// archetypes: Recorded transformer configurations (RFC 0019.13 §12.3). Decode and prefill are the same operation and different problems -- seqlen_q of 1 against a long cache is memory bound, and a square prefill is compute bound -- so each is anchored separately rather than left to a range over seqlen_q.
// neighbourhood: head_dim is absent on purpose: it takes one of a few values fixed by the model architecture, and an interpolated 96 or 112 is not a configuration anyone ships. seqlen_k mirrors seqlen_q at ratios >= 1, which keeps the declared seqlen_q <= seqlen_k relation satisfied by construction rather than by rejection.
// mixture: Same shares as conv_fwd; see the note there.
